quotes.text: Never get too comfortable. Even when everything seems to be going perfectly, stay vigilant, be ready to pivot, and don't be afraid to adjust the plan.
In the vineyard, adaptability is just as important as having a good plan in the first place.
Canada's greatest strength isn't trying to be like everyone else. It's producing wines with an identity that's unmistakably Canadian.
There is always something waiting in the shadows.

facts.fact: Monte Creek Winery is in the Thompson Valley, BC, near Kamloops; founded 2015; about 30,000 cases a year

Jesse Steinley has more than 20 years in vines and wine; he started as a dishwasher at an Ontario winery in his mid-teens, studied audio engineering planning to be a rock star, then followed someone across the country to a harvest job in BC
Winemaking style: elegant, acid and fruit driven wines that let the fruit express itself rather than hide the terroir

The 2025 vintage note: the northern latitude, once considered a disadvantage, has become one of Monte Creek's greatest strengths; Kamloops fruit stays on the vine longer, with cooler nights and shorter days
2023 was the biggest harvest Monte Creek has had in the Thompson Valley, in a year when the BC industry lost nearly 60% of its crop to a winter cold snap
Frontenac Gris is the best-selling wine in the tasting room
Jesse's one-bottle pick is the 2025 Living Land Frontenac Gris; the wine he thinks people underestimate is the Ancient Waters Riesling
Cold-tolerant varieties, geotextiles and burying the vines protect the Thompson Valley vineyards through winter

wines.name: Ancient Waters Riesling

specs.vineyard: Monte Creek Ranch and Lion's Head Vineyard

wines.winery_words: 100% Riesling, four months in stainless steel. Grown on scuitto soil, deep glaciolacustrine silty loam over volcanic bedrock. The 2022 season was a slow burn: acids stayed high well into harvest (spec sheet). Jesse: the most underestimated wine in the lineup, bright, crisp and beautifully balanced, with lively acidity and fresh citrus and orchard fruit; not sweet (interview).

expert_notes.nose: Sweet lime and jasmine aromas, with hints of guava and starfruit.
expert_notes.palate: Zesty citrus rushes the palate, bursting with lime, grapefruit and lemon drop. Light to medium bodied, and loaded with powerful, invigorating acidity. Some soft salinity adds depth on a long finish.
expert_notes.notes: This low-alcohol wine is perfect for wine lovers seeking acidity driven wines.
expert_notes.pairing: Lemon meringue pie, pineapple upside down cake, lemon tarts; roasted chicken, French fries, corn chowder, smoked applewood cheddar.

expert_notes.appearance: A pale clear gold in the glass.
expert_notes.nose: The delicious scent of diesel is the first sense that hit the nose. Followed by some pleasant tangy citrus, white grapefruit and a touch of kiwi, finishing with light brioche.
expert_notes.palate: The palate follows the nose with the diesel and citrus mingle together with a base of acidity. Smooth and with some depth.
expert_notes.pairing: Charcuterie and an assortment of soft cheeses.

expert_notes.text: Very pale straw with a greenish hue; minerally, lime bouquet; light-bodied, elegant, lime and grapefruit flavours with just a suggestion of honey to balance the rush of acidity.
expert_notes.pairing: Baked ham; smoked salmon; pork risotto.

wines.pairing: Leah: lemon tarts, roasted chicken, smoked applewood cheddar. Valerie: charcuterie and soft cheeses. Tony: smoked salmon.
wines.role: Jesse's most underestimated wine; the one wine the winery says is close to stocking out at 1,600 members

page_note.vineyard: Monte Creek Ranch and Lion's Head Vineyard
page_note.style: A traditional, flavourful, low-alcohol Riesling: fresh, smooth and acidity-driven, with some depth. Winemaker Jesse Steinley calls it the most underestimated wine in the lineup, a reminder that Riesling is not always sweet.
page_note.score_line: 92. Four months in stainless steel. Riesling benefits from a little air, so let it lose its chill for a few minutes.
page_note.appearance: A pale, clear gold in the glass.
page_note.nose: Diesel comes first, then tangy citrus, white grapefruit and a touch of kiwi, finishing with light brioche.
page_note.palate: Diesel and citrus mingle over a base of acidity; stone fruit shows as the wine sits. Smooth and a little richer as it warms, with some depth.
page_note.extra: Grown on scuitto soil, deep glaciolacustrine silty loam over volcanic bedrock. The 2022 season was a slow burn, so acids stayed high into harvest. 346 cases were made.

wines.name: Living Land Cabernet Franc
wines.winery_words: 88% Cabernet Franc, 12% Merlot, 15 months in French oak. Sweetly exuberant with snappy candied cherries and luscious spice, well-integrated oak; structured through to the finish with chewy tannins. Bottled July 2025. 1,300 cases.

expert_notes.nose: Intensely perfumed with violets, black caps, cherry, vanilla, nutmeg
expert_notes.palate: Bright, black raspberry, pepper and purple plum notes are married with warm, toasty oak and baking spice notes: cedar, nutmeg, vanilla. Full-bodied, well-balanced, and beautiful concentrated fruit that is balanced with good oak integration. The tannins are ripe, granular and sand-like which reveals this wine would still reward further aging (5-10 years). Dark chocolate notes approach on a long finish.
expert_notes.pairing: T-bone steak, hot roast-beef sandwiches, turkey dinners, charcuterie boards, gouda, mozzarella, roasted root veggies, Chinese food.

expert_notes.text: Deep purple in colour; spicy, vanilla and black cherry nose; medium to full-bodied, dry, well extracted black cherry and black plum flavours with a firm finish of ripe tannins. Well-integrated oak. Hold 1 - 2 years.

wines.pairing: Grilled vegetables and herb-rubbed halloumi or roasted poultry (winery). Leah: T-bone steak, roast turkey.

page_note.style: Full-bodied and well balanced, with concentrated fruit and good oak integration. The tannins are ripe, granular and sand-like.

wines.name: Living Land Frontenac Gris Organic
wines.winery_words: 100% Frontenac Gris, four months in stainless steel, bottled February 26, 2026. Herbaceous nose, fresh gooseberry and candied citrus; pineapple, mango, tangerine. The best-selling wine in the tasting room. Jesse's pick if members open only one bottle: bright, refreshing, easy-drinking, and very few wineries grow Frontenac Gris (interview).

expert_notes.appearance: A light yellow with a very slight green tinge but clear as crystal as it shimmers in the glass.
expert_notes.nose: The scents of the wine are beyond heavenly, floral with fresh pear and underlying citrus, some honey notes. Faint essence of freshly chopped parsley adds interest to the clean, pure aromas as the wine sits in the glass. The tiniest hint of oak.
expert_notes.palate: On the palate the first thing that hits is the richness of the oak that follows from the nose. Beautifully lush but never heavy nor too crisp. Enticingly fresh and the citrus keeps it tight. This is an incredibly refreshing wine. Focused with an acidity that never quits.
expert_notes.pairing: Fabulous on its own; fresh seafood, scallop crudo, Dungeness crab.

expert_notes.text: Tasted as the 2022 vintage: pale straw colour; earthy, green melon bouquet; medium-bodied, dry, spicy, tangerine flavour; lively acidity, lovely mouth feel.
expert_notes.pairing: Seafood dishes; soft cheeses; lobster rolls.
expert_notes.vintage_note: 2022 vintage, not the 2025: do not quote

wines.pairing: General spicy dishes (winery). Valerie: scallop crudo, Dungeness crab.

page_note.style: Lush but never heavy, and never too crisp: a refreshing, focused wine with acidity that never quits. Best-selling wine in the winery's tasting room, and winemaker Jesse Steinley's pick if you open only one bottle.
page_note.score_line: 92. Four months in stainless steel. Awards: 89 points, Gismondi on Wine (lineup sheet).
page_note.appearance: A light yellow with a very slight green tinge, clear as crystal.
page_note.nose: Floral, with fresh pear, underlying citrus and honey notes. A faint essence of freshly chopped parsley and the tiniest hint of oak. The winery adds gooseberry and candied citrus.
page_note.palate: The richness of oak leads, then lush, fresh fruit with citrus keeping it tight. Pineapple, mango and tangerine from the winery's notes. It gets more flavourful as it sits.
page_note.serving: 8–10 °C. Beautiful straight from the fridge, richer after a few minutes.
page_note.extra: Few wineries grow Frontenac Gris, so this is a chance to try a new varietal. Bottled February 26, 2026. 545 cases were made.

wines.name: Ancient Waters Rosé

oak.claim: 50% saignée Pinot Noir, 24 hours on skins before part of the juice is bled off

wines.winery_words: 100% Pinot Noir, 50% saignée. Fresh strawberry and ripe cherry, honeysuckle; strawberry, juicy raspberry, sweet cherry; fresh and silky. 202 cases.

expert_notes.appearance: Beautiful crystal rose colour, somewhere between pale and shimmering. Very attractive in the glass, a rose gold. Like a jewel.
expert_notes.nose: Wild strawberry mixed with light floral and a touch of Jolly Rancher with an almond finish.
expert_notes.palate: A serious wine, far from what I expected. Firm, with an amazingly tantalizing body that hits close to medium without any evidence of heaviness. This is not your aunt's Rosé: bright and vibrant. Flavours of fresh cranberry provide the backbone.
